title: Rejecting an auto-awarded report does not reverse its evidence award or release the award claim

original_titles.title: Reviewer rejection does not reverse auto-awarded points or release the award claim
reverses_entry_id never used in production code paths

problem: The auto-matcher can claim an award unit and write evidence_report points before human review. The reject_invalid branch of apply_review_outcome only updates submission status to decided; it does not append a reversal entry or remove/release the award_claims row. reverses_entry_id is not used on this code path.
impact: A report later rejected by a reviewer can keep its automatic points and block a legitimate report for the same award unit. Final scores remain wrong unless a manual adjustment is made.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Fetch all award ledger entries for the submission and award_claims row inside the same transaction that records the final reject decision.
Append a reversal ledger entry for each awarded component with points equal to the exact inverse and reverses_entry_id pointing to the original entry. Do not delete history.
Release the award claim using a compare-and-delete/update predicate tied to the same submission_id; never release a claim that has been reassigned.
Make the rejection handler idempotent so a retry cannot create duplicate reversals. Update submission status and audit the reviewer, original award ids and reversal ids atomically.
Add integration tests: auto-match -> evidence award -> reviewer reject -> reversal -> another valid submission can claim the unit; repeat the job and verify no duplicate ledger entry.

acceptance_criteria: Rejected reports have net zero score for the rejected award.
The award claim is available for a later valid submission.
The ledger remains append-only and reversals are traceable.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
